audit.whatIsWrong: The chart sides are right, but whys[3], whys[4] and whys[5] name the wrong stages — 'Level 4', 'Level 5', 'Level 6' against rows labelled Levels 4-5, Level 6, First item.
audit.why: phases[].side and win[] already match the packet (Graves, Skill, Yasuo, Yasuo, Graves, Yasuo, Yasuo) and the mirror, so no side flips are needed. The prose labels are simply off by one stage, which makes the chart read as if Level 6 goes to Yasuo when the row says Graves.
audit.corrected: whys[3..5] relabelled to Levels 4-5 / Level 6 / First item, keeping the existing sides.

audit.why: End of the Line 13/11.25/9.5/7.75/6, Smoke Screen 26/24/22/20/18, Quickdraw 16/15/14/13/12, Collateral Damage 100/80/60, Wind Wall 25s at rank 1 for 4s, Last Breath 70/50/30.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into whys[4], early, spikes[1], late, phases[4].why, breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Smoke Screen is described as blinding your autos; Wind Wall is pointed at Quickdraw; and 'Last Breath converts ANY knockup'.
audit.why: Riot's text for Smoke Screen is 'creates a cloud of smoke that reduces sight range' plus a brief slow — it is sight denial, not a blind, so your autos still land if you can see him. Quickdraw is a dash, which Wind Wall cannot stop. The decisive interaction the page never states: Graves' basic attacks are projectiles ('Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units'), so Wind Wall deletes his auto damage outright — that is the single biggest lever in the matchup, and the mirror flagged it too. Last Breath needs an airborne target, and nothing in Graves' kit lifts him, so your own two-stack Steel Tempest whirlwind is the only setup.
audit.corrected: Smoke Screen reframed as sight denial; Wind Wall pointed at his bullets and End of the Line; Q2 whirlwind named as the only Last Breath setup.

edits.before: Level 4 stays yours since you punish every reload window while glued to him.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay yours since you punish every reload window while glued to him.

edits.before: Level 5 swings back to Graves as his combo damage spikes and out-trades you if he lands it.
edits.after: Level 6 swings back to Graves — Collateral Damage is 100s but it out-trades you if it lands.

edits.before: Level 6 is Yasuo's because Last Breath catches him mid-reload with no ranged escape.
edits.after: First item is Yasuo's: Last Breath catches him mid-reload with no ranged escape.

edits.before: Graves has no ranged escape at 6; catch him mid-reload with Q3 knock-up into R before he can Quickdraw (E) dash away.
edits.after: Collateral Damage is 100s at rank 1 and he has no ranged escape — catch him mid-reload with the Q2 whirlwind into R.

edits.before: Your crit spike out-trades his burst up close, but a well-placed Smoke Screen blinds your autos — Wind Wall his End of the Line and E onto him through the smoke edge.
edits.after: Your crit spike out-trades his burst up close. Wind Wall blocks his basic attacks too — all four bullets — so drop it on his reload and walk him down through the smoke.

edits.before: Late Graves hits hard if he lands his full shell burst from range; stay on top of him, Wind Wall the Q, and force the reload window.
edits.after: Late Graves hits hard from range; stay on top of him and use Wind Wall on his reload — it eats his bullets outright — then force the gap.

edits.before: Graves owns Level 1 — his two-shell burst and End of the Line (Q) out-range and out-trade you before you have a dash. Play safe, respect the Smoke Screen blind, and don't walk into his point-blank shotgun.
edits.after: Graves owns Level 1 — his shell burst and End of the Line (Q, 13s at rank 1) out-range you before you have a dash. Smoke Screen cuts your sight, it does not blind you, so hold position and keep last-hitting.

edits.before: From 6 you're favored: catch him mid-reload with Q3 into Last Breath before Quickdraw resets. With items you win up close but must Wind Wall his End of the Line and eat through the Smoke Screen — force the reload gap and he folds.
edits.after: From 6 you're favoured: catch him mid-reload with the Q2 whirlwind into Last Breath before Quickdraw (16s at rank 1) resets. Wind Wall deletes every projectile he owns, his autos included — force the reload gap and he folds.

edits.before: Last Breath converts ANY knockup into a kill window. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Graves's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Last Breath (70s at rank 1) fires only off your own Q2 whirlwind. Collateral Damage is 100s — bait it before you commit.

edits.before: Last Breath converts ANY knockup into a kill window — build your teamfight around that. Graves carry threat: 8/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Last Breath needs an airborne target and only your own Q2 whirlwind supplies one. Graves carry threat: 8/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.

edits.before: - Graves Quickdraw: matchup-defining — His dash + armor stacks. Engage when it's down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Graves Quickdraw: 16s at rank 1 — his dash plus True Grit resists. Engage inside that gap. - End of the Line is 13s, and Wind Wall eats it along with his autos. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: His dash + armor stacks. Engage when it's down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His dash plus True Grit resists, 16s at rank 1 — engage inside that window, not before.

edits.before: Graves wastes Quickdraw — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Wind Wall stops all four of his bullets — his autos included.

notes: Chart sides were already correct in both layers; only the whys[] stage labels were off by one. The high-value fix here is that Graves' basic attacks are projectiles, so Wind Wall blanks his auto damage — the page previously pointed the wall at Quickdraw, which is a dash.
